title.narrative: Strengthening Human Rights and Peace Research and Education in ASEAN/Southeast Asia – SHAPE-SEA
โครงการเสริมสร้างความเข้มแข็งด้านการวิจัยสิทธิมนุษยชนและสันติศึกษาในอาเซียน/เอเชียตะวันออกเฉียงใต้ ระยะที่ 2

description.narrative: SHAPE-SEA (Strengthening Human Rights and Peace Research and Education in ASEAN/Southeast Asia) is a regional programme that strengthens human rights and peace research and education in Southeast Asia. It builds the capacity of scholars, universities, and civil society actors through research grants, training, mentoring, knowledge production, publication, and regional dissemination. The programme supports homegrown research and education on human rights and peace, and promotes collaboration among academic institutions, civil society, and regional stakeholders across ASEAN/Southeast Asia.

โครงการเสริมสร้างความเข้มแข็งด้านการวิจัยสิทธิมนุษยชนและสันติศึกษาในอาเซียน/เอเชียตะวันออกเฉียงใต้ ระยะที่ 2 (Strengthening Human Rights and Peace Research and Education in ASEAN/Southeast Asia – SHAPE-SEA) ดำเนินงานโดยสถาบันสิทธิมนุษยชนและสันติศึกษา มหาวิทยาลัยมหิดล ภายใต้สัญญาความร่วมมือ “Grant Agreement between The Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, SIDA and Mahidol University regarding SHAPE-SEA Phase 2”, Sida Contribution No. 12124

participating-org.narrative: Institute of Human Rights and Peace Studies, Mahidol University

recipient-region.narrative: SHAPE-SEA is designed to serve the ten ASEAN member states (Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam) as well as the broader Southeast Asian region.

sector.narrative: SHAPE-SEA is reported under 15160 — Human rights (100%) as its primary OECD DAC sector. Within this overall human rights objective, the programme also contributes to related thematic areas, including 11420 — Higher education through research training, mentoring, academic capacity-building, and support to scholars and universities; 15150 — Democratic participation and civil society through work on civic space, public participation, academic freedom, and civil society engagement; 15130 — Legal and judicial development through research on justice, rule of law, legal protection, and accountability; 15220 — Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution through research, education, and dialogue on peace, conflict transformation, and regional peacebuilding; 15170 — Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions through work engaging gender equality, women’s rights, feminist movements, and gender justice; and 41010 — Environmental policy and administrative management through research and dissemination on environmental rights, climate justice, and environmental governance. These codes are not reported as separate sector percentages, but reflect important programming dimensions under SHAPE-SEA’s broader human rights framework.
